title: Compounding of offences - which cases can genuinely be settled
p1:
Not every criminal case has to end in a long courtroom battle.

But here is the surprising part: many people think any case can be settled if both sides agree. That is not how the law works.
p2:
Compounding of offences means the law allows certain offences to be settled between the accused and the victim, usually with the victim accepting compensation or resolution. However, only specific offences can be compounded because some crimes are considered too serious to be treated as private disputes.

A simple cheque bounce matter or a minor personal dispute may have a path for settlement, but serious offences affecting society generally cannot be closed just because parties reach an agreement.
p3:
The key lesson: a compromise between two people does not automatically erase criminal liability. The nature of the offence decides whether settlement is legally possible.

Before assuming a case can be withdrawn, check whether the offence is legally compoundable and whether court permission is required.
conclusion: Have you ever seen a case where both sides wanted to settle but the law did not allow it? What was the reason?
